ipa-healthcheck on replica3-ops is UNKNOWN because the check plugin could not be found. Its output names /home/icinga/monitoring-scripts/monitoring/ipa/check_ipa_health.sh, and that path does not exist in rhpds/rhdp-monitoring -- fetching it fails.

Searching the repository for check_ipa_health.sh finds it at checks/identity/ipa/check_ipa_health.sh. The script itself is intact: it checks replication agreements and the CA subsystem, and it warns at a replication lag of 300 seconds and goes critical at 900 seconds.

So what is wrong is the check's own configuration, not IPA. The check_command still points at the old monitoring/ipa/ location after the script was moved under checks/identity/ipa/, so the plugin is never executed. Until that path is updated the service will stay UNKNOWN, and note that this tells us nothing at all about the replica's actual health -- the check has not run.
